'''Anne-Sophie Kaloghiros''' is a [[mathematics]] researcher in [[algebraic geometry]] and reader in Mathematics at [[Brunel University London]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.brunel.ac.uk/people/anne-sophie-kaloghiros|title=Dr Anne-Sophie Kaloghiros|work=People|publisher=Brunel University London|access-date=2024-01-31}}</ref> Kaloghiros was awarded the [[London Mathematical Society|London Mathematical Society (LMS)]] [[Emmy Noether Fellowship]] in 2020.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=LMS Emmy Noether Fellows 2020 Announced {{!}} London Mathematical Society|url=https://www.lms.ac.uk/news-entry/09072020-1421/lms-emmy-noether-fellows-2020-announced|access-date=2022-02-06|website=www.lms.ac.uk}}</ref>

== Professional career ==
Kaloghiros earned her BA in pure mathematics (honours) from the [[Paris-Sud University|Université d’Orsay, Paris XI]] in 2001, a Degree of the [[École Centrale Paris|Ecole Centrale Paris]] in 2003, and a Certificate of Advanced Studies in Mathematics, Part III (Distinction) at [[Queens' College, Cambridge|Queens’ College]], [[University of Cambridge]] in 2003 as well.{{citation needed|date=March 2022}}

Kaloghiros earned her PhD in [[Algebraic geometry|Algebraic Geometry]] from [[University of Cambridge]] in 2007. Her dissertation, ''The Topology of Terminal Quartic 3-Folds'', was supervised by [[Alessio Corti]].<ref>{{mathgenealogy|126446}}</ref> She was a junior research fellow, [[Trinity Hall, Cambridge|Trinity Hall, University of Cambridge]] 2007–2011,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Trinity Hall Cambridge Newsletter |url=https://www.trinhall.cam.ac.uk/wp-content/uploads/2018/07/Newsletter-2007e.pdf}}</ref> a postdoctoral fellow, [[University of Cambridge]] in 2011, and research associate, [[Imperial College London]] 2012–2014. She has held visiting and postdoctoral positions at the [[Mathematical Sciences Research Institute]] (MSRI, Berkeley) in 2009 and 2019,<ref>{{Cite web |last=MSRI |title=Mathematical Sciences Research Institute |url=http://www.msri.org/ |access-date=2022-03-12 |website=www.msri.org}}</ref> at the [[Research Institute for Mathematical Sciences]] (RIMS, Kyoto University) 2009–2010, [[University of Illinois Chicago|University of Illinois at Chicago]] in 2011, and the [[Hausdorff Center for Mathematics|Hausdorff Research Institute for Mathematics]] (HIM, Bonn, Germany) in 2014. She is currently a senior lecturer in Maths/Op at [[Brunel University London]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Dr Anne-Sophie Kaloghiros |url=https://www.brunel.ac.uk/people/anne-sophie-kaloghiros |access-date=March 12, 2022 |website=Brunel University London}}</ref> She is an expert on [[algebraic geometry]] and [[birational geometry]]. She serves on the [[London Mathematical Society]] Mentoring African Research in Mathematics (MARM) board.<ref>{{Cite web |title=MARM Board {{!}} London Mathematical Society |url=https://www.lms.ac.uk/MARMBoard |access-date=2022-03-12 |website=www.lms.ac.uk}}</ref>

== Awards and honors ==
Kaloghiros received the Brunel Athena Swan Award for 2017–2018.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Research grants and contracts awarded |url=https://www.brunel.ac.uk/research/Centres/Mathematical-and-Statistical-Modelling/Research-grants-and-contracts-awarded |access-date=2022-03-12 |website=www.brunel.ac.uk |language=en-GB}}</ref> In 2020, she was awarded the [[London Mathematical Society|London Mathematical Society (LMS)]] [[Emmy Noether Fellowship]].<ref name=":0" /> Her research has been funded by the [[Heilbronn Institute for Mathematical Research]], [[Engineering and Physical Sciences Research Council|the Engineering and Physical Sciences Research Council (EPSRC)]], the [[London Mathematical Society]], [[Edinburgh Mathematical Society]], and [[Glasgow Mathematical Journal|Glasgow Mathematical Journal Trust]].
